transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I'm here because for a long time now, my sleep has just been broken. I fall into bed completely exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then... I'm just up before the alarm even goes off, feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried even when you're not thinking about your sleep?

No, not really. I mean... I don't feel particularly anxious or worried during the day. I don't sit around stressing about things out of nowhere, if that's what you mean. It's mostly just that I feel so drained from not getting any real rest.
Do you have trouble falling asleep at the beginning of the night, or does sleep come easily but then get disrupted later?

Well, falling asleep isn't usually the problem. Like I said, I fall into bed just completely exhausted from the day. It's staying asleep that's the issue. I'll drop off fine, but then... yeah, every little noise wakes me up, and once I'm up, that's pretty much it. I'm just lying there until morning, not really resting at all.
Even on nights when you have plenty of time in bed and aren’t disturbed, do you still wake up feeling unrefreshed?

I'm... I'm not really sure. I can't really remember the last time I had a night where I wasn't disturbed or didn't wake up in the middle of it. It happens pretty much every time I go to bed. So, I don't really know how I'd feel if I actually got to sleep straight through without any interruptions.
Have you ever noticed that even on nights when you aren’t disturbed and sleep through the night, you still wake up feeling tired or unrefreshed?

Like I was just saying, I really don't have nights where I sleep all the way through. That's actually why I'm here. My sleep has been broken for a long time now. I fall into bed completely exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. Once I'm awake, I'm just up, usually way before my alarm even goes off, and I feel like I never really rested at all. So, I don't know what it's like to sleep through the night anymore.
Even if you manage to sleep through the night without waking up, do you still wake up feeling tired or like you haven't had restful sleep?

Doctor, I... I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I said, I don't manage to sleep through the night. That just doesn't happen for me anymore. Every night is the same—I wake up, and then I'm awake for good. So I really can't tell you how I'd feel if I slept straight through, because I just don't.
Have you ever taken a nap during the day, even a long one, and still felt unrefreshed afterward?

I don't really get the chance to take naps during the day with my work schedule. But I can tell you that the tiredness just never really lifts. By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and come back to help out at my own house... my body just feels so heavy. It gets to the point where even just sitting down to chart my notes, or trying to fold a load of laundry, it can feel like too much to push through. So I don't think a nap would even fix it at this point.
Let’s say you take a nap or have a day off where you can sleep as long as you want—do you ever wake up feeling refreshed, or do you still feel just as tired as before you slept?

Doctor, I know we just talked about this. Like I said, I don't really get to take naps or sleep as long as I want. But I can tell you that the tiredness doesn't go away. When I get done with my home-health clients and get home, my body just feels... heavy. Just sitting down to do my charting or trying to fold some laundry feels like it's too much to push through. So, no, I don't think sleeping longer would make me feel refreshed.
Even when you sleep for a long time, do you still wake up feeling like you haven't rested at all?

Doctor, I... I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again. Like I've been saying, I don't get to sleep for a long time. But the tiredness is just always there. After I'm done seeing my home-health clients for the day and I get back to my own house, my body is just so heavy. It's like... even sitting down to finish my charting, or just trying to fold some laundry, it feels like way too much to push through. It doesn't matter what I do, I'm just always exhausted.
If you sleep for a long time, either at night or during the day, do you still wake up feeling like you haven’t rested at all?

I... I really don't know how else to explain this to you. We've gone over this a few times now. I don't get the chance to sleep for a long time. But the fatigue, it just doesn't stop. Like I said, when I'm done with my home-health clients and I get back to my house... my body is just incredibly heavy. Just sitting down to do my charting, or, you know, trying to fold a load of laundry... it just feels like too much to push through. I'm just always tired, no matter what.
Have you ever had a chance to sleep for a full night without any interruptions, and if so, did you wake up feeling rested or still tired?

Doctor, I really don't know what else to say. I feel like we are just going in circles here. Like I've been trying to tell you, even if I do get a full night of sleep, it doesn't change anything. By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and come back to my own house, my body just feels so heavy. Just doing the basics, like finishing my charting notes or trying to fold the laundry... it just feels like way too much to push through. The tiredness never goes away, no matter how I sleep.
Have you ever had a night where you slept for a normal or long amount of time and still woke up feeling as though you hadn’t rested at all?

I... I honestly don't know how to answer this any differently, Doctor. You are asking me the exact same question again. 

Yes. Even if I get a normal amount of sleep, I still wake up tired. Like I've been trying to tell you, it doesn't matter how I sleep. By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and come back to my own house, my body just feels incredibly heavy. Even the smallest things, like finishing my charting notes or trying to fold some laundry... it just feels like way too much to push through. The exhaustion is just always there.
